core_obligations: Reduce to comparing sections (proof lines 2539-2560): the blowup is the projective spectrum of the Rees algebra, hence integral and projective over the base; let the normalization be finite because the ring is Nagata, and let the inverse image of the exceptional divisor be the pullback of the ideal sheaf of the exceptional divisor, an effective Cartier divisor; since the normalization is finite it suffices to show that the structure sheaf of the blowup maps isomorphically to its pushforward.

Suppose the comparison fails (proof lines 2560-2566): if the map on structure sheaves were not an isomorphism, then by the recovery of modules from their associated graded along an ample invertible sheaf there would be an index where the sections of the corresponding twists differ.

Compute both sides (proof lines 2568-2576): the sections of the pushforward twisted by the power of the exceptional ideal equal the sections of the pullback of that twist on the normalization, which by the chapter's computation are exactly the powers of the maximal ideal; on the other hand the powers of the maximal ideal inject into the sections of the twist on the blowup, and since the latter are torsion free the inclusion is an equality for all indices, so the two associated graded modules agree and the normalization is an isomorphism.
proof_roadmap: Identify the blowup as a projective integral modification and the exceptional divisor as an effective Cartier divisor pulled back along the normalization.
Use ampleness to reduce the equality of structure sheaves to an equality of sections of all twists.
Compute the sections on both sides using the rational singularity input and conclude.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that in the rational singularity situation the blowup of the spectrum of the ring in its maximal ideal is normal (statement lines 2533-2537). The proof (proof lines 2539-2578) identifies the blowup with the projective spectrum of the Rees algebra, reduces the normality of the blowup to an isomorphism between the structure sheaf and the pushforward along the finite normalization, and verifies the required equality of sections of all twists by computing both sides through the rational singularity input. H3: an original comparison of sections with a genuine ample-module argument, written out in full.
